text:
The dominant regulatory story this week is the EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR), whose core obligations entered into binding legal effect on 12 August 2026. Multiple items converge on this date: the Declaration of Conformity requirement and PFAS restrictions now in force, transport-packaging requirements affecting green and roasted coffee shipments, and the Commission's new implementation guidance (Notice C/2026/3702) alongside its FAQ clarifications. Given JDE Peet's packaged portfolio — Jacobs, L'OR, Senseo, Tassimo, Douwe Egberts, Kenco, Pickwick, Moccona — is named directly in several of these items as subject to design-for-recycling and extended producer responsibility rules, compliance exposure here is immediate rather than prospective.

On deforestation compliance, the EU Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) enforcement deadline of 30 December 2026 remains the other major regulatory fixture, requiring geolocation-based due diligence and deforestation-free certification for coffee sourcing. Hungary's food safety authority (NEBIH) resumed EUDR training for importers after a system outage, and the European Coffee Federation held a high-level EUDR dialogue with producing-country representatives at World of Coffee in Brussels — both signaling that implementation friction persists industry-wide as the deadline approaches, which suggests continued uncertainty for upstream suppliers rather than a settled compliance path.

On the corporate/competitive side, Keurig Dr Pepper's Q2 2026 results (reported 6 August 2026) showed JDE Peet's contributing $2.8 billion in sales within KDP's 75.6% year-over-year net sales growth, despite disappointing U.S. coffee performance; KDP reaffirmed full-year guidance and its plan to separate into Beverage Co. and Global Coffee Co. in early 2027. KDP's board appointment of Aaron Alt (Cardinal Health CFO, ex-Sysco) was explicitly framed around preparing for this separation, reinforcing that the post-acquisition corporate restructuring is proceeding on schedule with JDE Peet's positioned as the core of the future Global Coffee Co.

On supply chain and trade, coffee markets showed continued volatility: shipments from Colombia's Buenaventura port partially resumed after disruptions, coinciding with a sharp 13 August drop in coffee futures (New York December contract -2.2%, London November -2.9%), which suggests markets are still absorbing supply-chain risk premia built up over recent months. Separately, the European Parliament's approval of the EU-US trade deal — capping US tariffs at 15% in exchange for eliminated EU tariffs on US goods — was flagged as relevant to KDP's transatlantic supply and cost structure, though its direct effect on JDE Peet's European operations is not yet quantified in the available reporting.
